blocks.text: It is exactly the opposite of the synthesis. It involves the breaking down of the target molecule into less complicated, simpler and more readily available compounds which can serve as starting material. Retrosynthesis involves the disconnection approach.

blocks.alt: Target Molecule on the left and Starting Material on the right, joined by two open retrosynthetic arrows pointing to the starting material. A magenta loop labelled Retrosynthesis runs over the top from the target molecule down to the starting material; a cyan loop labelled Synthesis runs round the bottom from the starting material back up to the target molecule.
blocks.caption: Figure 25.1: Synthesis and retrosynthesis routes (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 25.1).

blocks.text: In retrosynthesis, those bonds of the target molecule are disconnected that result in a considerable structural simplification. Following a series of disconnections, we shall eventually arrive at simple, easily available starting materials.

items: Retrosynthetic arrow is an open-ended arrow and denoted by ⇒.
Target Molecule (TM) is the molecule which is to be prepared by disconnection.
Disconnection is a process which involves the imaginary breaking down of the TM progressively into simpler starting materials.
Synthons are fragments of the target molecule which are generated by a disconnection. They are often an ionic species and represent the building blocks for the synthesis.
Synthetic Equivalent (SE) is a reagent used to carry out the function of a synthon which cannot be used itself because it is usually unstable.
Functional Group Interconversion (FGI) is the conversion of one functional group into another to reach the target molecule.
Retrosynthetic Tree is a diagram showing all possible disconnections and synthons from the target molecule to starting materials.

blocks.text: Figure 25.2 shows all the terminologies in a single scheme.

blocks.alt: Aniline (benzene ring with NH2), labelled Target Molecule (TM), with an open arrow labelled FGI to nitrobenzene, whose C-N bond is crossed by a wavy slash. A cyan open arrow labelled Disconnection splits into two arrows: up to synthon (A), a benzene ring with a negative charge, equivalent to benzene (SE); and down to synthon (B), NO2 with a positive charge, equivalent to HNO3, nitric acid (SE).
blocks.caption: Figure 25.2: Terminologies used in retrosynthesis (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 25.2).
